title: Enhancing Automated Unit Test Generation with Large Language Models: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Zhang J, Hu X, Gao C, Xia X, Li S
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
abstract: Automated unit test generation is a fundamental yet challenging task in software engineering, playing a critical role in ensuring software correctness, reliability, and maintainability. While traditional approaches such as search-based software testing have been widely studied, the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has opened new research directions. This paper presents a systematic literature review on LLM-based automated unit test generation, analyzing trends, techniques, evaluation metrics including coverage and mutation score, and open challenges.

title: Benchmarking LLMs for Unit Test Generation from Real-World Functions
authors: Dong Huang, Jie M. Zhang, Mark Harman, Qianru Zhang, Mingzhe Du, See-Kiong Ng
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
abstract: Recently, large language models (LLMs) have shown great promise in automating unit test generation, significantly reducing the manual effort required by developers. Existing LLM test generation benchmarks are limited by two critical drawbacks: data contamination and structurally simple function code. To address these problems, we introduce ULT (UnLeakedTestbench), a new benchmark specifically designed for function-level unit test generation from real-world Python functions, constructed through a multi-stage curation process ensuring high cyclomatic complexity and mitigating test case contamination.

title: Beyond Coverage: Automatic Test Suite Augmentation for Enhanced Effectiveness using Large Language Models
authors: Zeyu Lu, Peng Zhang, Yuge Nie, Yibiao Yang, Yutian Tang, Chun Yong Chong, Yuming Zhou
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages (OOPSLA1)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have gained significant traction in software engineering for automating tasks such as unit test generation. Most existing studies prioritize code coverage as the primary metric for enhancing test suite effectiveness. However, prior research has shown that although code coverage can reach approximately 80%, the mutation score, which generally exhibits a stronger correlation with defect detection effectiveness, attains only about 35%. This gap highlights the need to enhance test suite effectiveness guided by mutation score rather than code coverage.

title: A Comprehensive Study on Large Language Models for Mutation Testing
authors: Wang B, Chen M, Deng M, Lin Y, Harman M, Papadakis M, Zhang J
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
abstract: Comprehensive empirical study on applying large language models to mutation testing tasks; systematically evaluates LLM effectiveness in generating mutants and killing mutants compared to traditional mutation testing tools.

title: Advancing Code Coverage: Incorporating Program Analysis with Large Language Models
authors: Yang C, Chen J, Lin B, Wang Z, Zhou J
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
abstract: Incorporates program analysis techniques with large language models to improve branch and code coverage in automated test generation; addresses hard-to-cover branches through static analysis-guided prompting.

title: Automated Unit Test Generation via Chain of Thought Prompt and Reinforcement Learning from Coverage Feedback
authors: Junwei Zhang, Xing Hu, Xin Xia, Shing-Chi Cheung, Shanping Li
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
abstract: Recently, large language models (LLMs) have shown promising results in code generation, and several automated test generation approaches based on LLMs have been proposed. Although these approaches achieve promising performance, they suffer from two limitations. This paper proposes TestCTRL, which uses chain-of-thought prompts and reinforcement learning from coverage feedback to improve LLM-based unit test generation, fine-tuning CodeLlama-7B with coverage-based rewards.

title: Automated Unit Test Improvement using Large Language Models at Meta
authors: Nadia Alshahwan, Jubin Chheda, Anastasia Finogenova, Beliz Gokkaya, Mark Harman, Inna Harper, Alexandru Marginean, Shubho Sengupta, Eddy Wang
venue: FSE 2024 – Companion Proceedings of the 32nd ACM International Conference on the Foundations of Software Engineering
abstract: Describes Meta's TestGen-LLM tool which uses LLMs to automatically improve existing human-written unit tests. TestGen-LLM verifies that its generated test classes successfully clear a set of filters that assure measurable improvement in code coverage and test quality over the original tests.

title: Evaluating and Improving ChatGPT for Unit Test Generation
authors: Zhiqiang Yuan, Yiling Lou, Mingwei Liu, Shiji Ding, Kaixin Wang, Yixuan Chen, Xin Peng
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (FSE)
abstract: This paper performs an empirical study to evaluate the capability of ChatGPT in unit test generation. The study measures syntactic correctness, compilation correctness, statement coverage, branch coverage, and mutation score of ChatGPT-generated tests versus EvoSuite and other baselines on Java projects.

title: Code-Aware Prompting: A Study of Coverage-Guided Test Generation in Regression Setting using LLM
authors: Gabriel Ryan, Siddhartha Jain, Mingyue Shang, Shiqi Wang, Xiaofei Ma, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Baishakhi Ray
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (FSE)
abstract: This paper presents SymPrompt, a code-aware prompting strategy for LLMs in test generation that deconstructs test suite generation into a multi-stage sequence driven by execution paths. The approach enables pretrained LLMs to generate more complete test cases without additional training, evaluated on open-source Python projects with significant branch coverage improvements.

title: Domain Adaptation for Code Model-Based Unit Test Case Generation
authors: Jiho Shin, Sepehr Hashtroudi, Hadi Hemmati, Song Wang
venue: ISSTA 2024 – 33rd ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
abstract: This study leverages Transformer-based code models to generate unit tests with domain adaptation at a project level. Using CodeT5 fine-tuned on test generation and then domain-adapted to target projects, the approach improves line coverage by ~19% and mutation score by ~16% compared to CodeT5 without DA, A3Test, and GPT-4 baselines on Defects4J.

title: CoverUp: Effective High Coverage Test Generation for Python
authors: Juan Altmayer Pizzorno, Emery D. Berger
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (FSE)
abstract: Testing is an essential part of software development. Test generation tools attempt to automate the otherwise labor-intensive task of test creation, but generating high-coverage tests remains challenging. This paper proposes CoverUp, a novel approach to driving the generation of high-coverage Python regression tests. CoverUp combines coverage analysis, code context, and feedback in prompts that iteratively guide the LLM to generate tests that improve line and branch coverage. Compared to CodaMosa, CoverUp achieves median line+branch coverage of 80% (vs. 47%).

title: CodaMosa: Escaping Coverage Plateaus in Test Generation with Pre-Trained Large Language Models
authors: Caroline Lemieux, Jeevana Priya Inala, Shuvendu K. Lahiri, Siddhartha Sen
venue: ICSE 2023 – 45th International Conference on Software Engineering
abstract: Search-based software testing (SBST) generates high-coverage test cases for programs under test with a combination of test case generation and mutation. This paper proposes CodaMosa, which escapes coverage plateaus by using a pre-trained large language model to generate test cases for under-covered functions, then seeding SBST with those examples.

title: An initial investigation of ChatGPT unit test generation capability
venue: SAST 2023 – 8th Brazilian Symposium on Systematic and Automated Software Testing
abstract: This paper investigates ChatGPT for automated Java unit test generation without human interference. Metrics including code line coverage, mutation score, and test execution success rate were collected to evaluate efficiency. Results show the OpenAI LLM test set demonstrated similar performance across all evaluated aspects compared to traditional automated Java test generation tools.

title: Optimizing Search-Based Unit Test Generation with Large Language Models: An Empirical Study
authors: Danni Xiao, Yimeng Guo, Yanhui Li, Lin Chen
abstract: Search-based unit test generation methods have been considered effective and widely applied, and Large Language Models (LLMs) have also demonstrated powerful generation ability. This paper explores the application of LLMs at various stages of search-based test generation including the initial stage, the test generation period, and the test coverage plateaus, investigating when and how LLMs should intervene in the time-consuming test generation process.

title: Mutation-Guided LLM-based Test Generation at Meta
authors: Mark Harman, Jillian Ritchey, Inna Harper, Shubho Sengupta, Ke Mao, Abhishek Gulati, Christopher Foster, Hervé Robert
venue: FSE Companion 2025 – 33rd ACM International Conference on the Foundations of Software Engineering
abstract: This paper describes Meta's Automated Compliance Hardening (ACH) system for mutation-guided LLM-based test generation. ACH generates relatively few mutants compared to traditional mutation testing, focusing on generating currently undetected faults specific to privacy concerns. Evaluated on 7 Meta platforms, ACH generated 571 additional unit tests with a 73% acceptance rate.

title: From Scenario to Code: Structured Prompting for LLM-Based Unit Test Generation
authors: (see paper – no full text via Basic ACM access)
venue: WSSE 2025 – 7th World Symposium on Software Engineering
abstract: Automated unit test generation is crucial for improving software quality. Existing tools such as EvoSuite exhibit limitations by generating tests that may lack readability and clarity, and may struggle to cover specific code branches. This paper proposes structured scenario-based prompting for LLM unit test generation, evaluated on SBST 2020 benchmark projects (GUAVA, SPOON, PDFBOX, FESCAR), achieving higher mutation score than EvoSuite while branch coverage remains slightly lower.

title: Test Intention Guided LLM-Based Unit Test Generation
authors: Nan Z, Guo Z, Liu K, Xia X
venue: ICSE 2025 – 47th International Conference on Software Engineering
abstract: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has accelerated the progress of intelligent software engineering technologies, which brings promising possibilities for unit test generation. This paper proposes a test intention guided approach that infers the intended behavior to be tested before generating unit tests, evaluated on branch coverage and mutation score metrics.

title: Effective Test Generation Using Pre-trained Large Language Models and Mutation Testing
authors: Arghavan Moradi Dakhel, Amin Nikanjam, Vahid Majdinasab, Foutse Khomh, Michel C. Desmarais
venue: Information and Software Technology (published via ACM DL)
abstract: Recently, researchers have leveraged Large Language Models (LLMs) of code to generate unit tests. While the code coverage of generated tests was usually assessed, the literature has acknowledged that coverage is weakly correlated with the efficiency of tests in bug detection. To improve over this limitation, this paper introduces MuTAP (Mutation Test case generation using Augmented Prompt), which improves test effectiveness by augmenting prompts with surviving mutants to expose limitations of generated test cases in detecting bugs.
